append.detail: Built 2026-11-16, dark behind HUNTS_CLAIMS_ENABLED. A team is a roster that shares one hunt_runs row, so the FH-006 key (run, stop) is one credit per team and stop. Migration 20270346072000_hunt_teams_editions.sql (not applied) adds hunt_teams, hunt_team_members and hunt_team_awards (service role only) and six commands: create (invite code stored as a hash), join, lock (opens the one run, clears the code), hunt_team_claim_apply (the door: checks the locked roster, then calls hunt_claim_apply unchanged), leave (the longest-standing member becomes captain and the run moves to them with its credits; the last member leaving disbands the team and withdraws the run) and award allocation (equal shares, spare units to the longest standing, written once per team and award). A BEFORE INSERT trigger on hunt_claims is the wall: a claim on a team run by anyone who is not an active member of a locked roster is refused whatever path wrote it. supabase/tests/hunt_teams.test.sql (34 assertions) proves an outsider and a departed member write nothing through the door, through hunt_claim_apply or by a raw row, and that two members proving one stop leave one progress row and one outbox event; it was run green against a local Postgres 16 with the Hunt migrations applied, not yet in CI against the real schema. lib/hunts/teams.ts holds the calls and the same split and succession rules for a screen to state; lib/hunts/team-store.ts reads the caller's own membership (a count, never a roster) and app/(main)/hunts/[slug]/play/team-actions.ts are the five actions. Requires FH-030 and FH-033 are still open: a team plays whatever graph the engine evaluates, so nothing here waits on them. The team screens, the scan route hand-off and the reward wiring moved to FH-043S.
